evidence_summary: M3-1/M2-1 to C4-3 increased permissible retail bulk and enabled a 257000-square-foot shopping center; the applicant limited floor area, height, uses and parking through a restrictive declaration and expanded wetland mitigation; CB unanimously approved and no one appeared at CPC.

evidence_summary: Special permit enabled a roughly 30000-square-foot museum expansion; CB approved 23-0 and the museum director alone spoke in support; a restrictive declaration committed the owner to Landmark Preservation Commission-approved maintenance and repair.

evidence_summary: Companion report documents CB approval limited to two of four parcels, 19 opponents including a councilmember and preservation groups, and 16 supporters; CPC approved all four parcels but required biosafety monitoring and selected partial ballroom preservation after public review.

evidence_summary: C6-1 to C5-4 raised base FAR from 6 to 10 for a 950000-square-foot tower; CB approved with traffic, transit, shadow, parking, affirmative-action and court-space concerns; CPC-driven revisions reduced height and bulk and widened the sidewalk, while some traffic impacts remained unmitigated.

evidence_summary: Special permits enabled the 950000-square-foot 330 Jay Street tower and 320-space garage; the report incorporates the companion map report documenting conditioned CB approval, 12 support speakers, CPC-driven design revisions and unmitigated traffic impacts.

evidence_summary: CB unanimously disapproved the 31-story office tower over the rail yard, citing displacement, scale, traffic, transit and open-space harms; one CPC opponent and three supporters appeared; CPC approved after a performance-space proposal, restroom access, an MTA agreement condition and environmental responses, while accepting significant unresolved impacts.

evidence_summary: Three-year renewal for an existing Penn Station amusement arcade; CB approved 31-0, BP approved and nobody appeared at CPC; no project change or substantive local issue is documented.

evidence_summary: The 12-block M1-1/M3-1-to-M1-1D action allowed limited residential expansion and replacement while retaining manufacturing controls; it began in response to local concern, and CB and BP requested city investigation and cleanup of contamination; CPC agreed and referred the cleanup request to DGS.

evidence_summary: A C1-2 overlay and street demapping enabled expansion of an existing shopping center; CB approved 19-11, BP approved and the applicant alone spoke at CPC; CPC required setbacks, landscaping and fencing through Restrictive Declaration D-142 to buffer nearby homes.
coder_notes: Eleven votes against an approval resolution are recorded as CB opposition votes but do not alone establish substantial organized opposition.

evidence_summary: A C1-2 overlay enabled a three-story mixed-use building on the applicant parcel and conformed existing commercial uses; CB approved 23-0, BP approved and nobody appeared at CPC.

evidence_summary: R7-2/R8 residential zoning changed to M1-4 to enable commercial and light-industrial development on five vacant urban-renewal sites; CB approved 31-2 and BP approved with screening and resident-communication conditions; CPC urged the agencies to consider them and investigate a requested text change rather than securing firm commitments.

evidence_summary: Special permit allowed continuing conversion between residential and transient-hotel uses within the existing Hotel Pierre; CB approved 22-0, BP approved and two speakers supported; no physical expansion or local controversy is documented.

evidence_summary: Special permit enabled conversion of a vacant 16-story cold-storage building to 74 lofts and retail; CB and BP approved and one project representative supported; remaining commercial tenants would be displaced with a required conversion contribution, and a restrictive declaration established landmark maintenance.

evidence_summary: Special permit allowed seven artist live-work units in long-vacant upper floors; CB approved 40-0, BP approved and one project representative supported; CPC found no tenants displaced and no excessive residential burden.

evidence_summary: Special permits enabled a 172805-square-foot nursing-home expansion and 273 net new beds; BP imposed extensive waterfront and landscaping conditions, which prompted revisions; a named community group and residents opposed size and traffic, but CPC approved after rejecting those concerns as insignificant.

evidence_summary: Special permit and related text amendment enabled a seasonal enclosed ice rink with 25 parking spaces; CB approved 34-0, BP approved and two speakers supported; CPC addressed traffic access and neighborhood character without documented local demands or opposition.

evidence_summary: Special permit enabled a 63790-square-foot cancer center; CB and BP approved with landmark, traffic and landscaping conditions; the owner agreed to investigate National Register eligibility and add plantings, while a Route 9A study addressed the requested traffic analysis.

evidence_summary: DCP removed three commercial overlays at the request of residents and CB 2 to preserve the residential use of two blocks; CB approved 30-0, BP approved and nobody appeared at CPC.

evidence_summary: Special permit added a 60-space accessory garage to an as-of-right 102-unit building already under construction; CB approved 37-0, BP approved and applicant counsel alone supported; CPC addressed parking supply and traffic.

evidence_summary: A C2-2 overlay enabled a 9569-square-foot retail development after CPC had rejected an earlier C8-1 proposal; CB approved 29-0 and BP approved with a rear-buffer condition, but the CPC report does not adopt or resolve that condition.

evidence_summary: CB4 and the BP conditioned approval on accessory-only signage; the applicant agreed and placed the sign specifications on the plans; CPC expressly adopted that response while finding limited traffic effects.

evidence_summary: The garage permit was integral to a 400-bed dormitory enabled by the companion rezoning; CB2 disapproved 18-15, the BP sought major height limits, and civic groups opposed the building as out of scale, but CPC approved after expressly rejecting those objections.
coder_notes: The selected report defers nearly all evidence to C 020097 ZMK. Civic organizations appeared on both sides; opposition is coded because the schema has no mixed category and organized opposition was substantial.

evidence_summary: CB4 approved 40-1 conditioned on nine trees; the applicant had committed to the trees and worked with the community on building design modifications; CPC credited those changes while approving the garage and floor-area exemption.
coder_notes: The as-of-right 259-unit building was already under construction. This action principally enables parking and exempts garage floor area, so development direction is none.

evidence_summary: The permit converts 18 floors to 45 apartments and funds landmark restoration; CB5 disapproved 15-7 over business displacement and neighborhood change, while the BP sought retention of ground-floor uses; CPC addressed the concerns, cited relocation and operating commitments, and approved.

evidence_summary: The permit legalized continued operation of an existing large variety store without enlargement; CB1 approved 35-0, the BP approved late, and only the applicant spoke; CPC substantively reviewed traffic and neighborhood compatibility.

evidence_summary: The permit replaced a 125-space lot with a six-story 219-space garage; CB5 and the BP approved, no one opposed at CPC, and CPC reviewed facade design, curb-cut reduction, pedestrian flow, and traffic.
coder_notes: A stand-alone parking structure is not coded as a material increase in housing or general development capacity under the codebook.

evidence_summary: The permit converted an existing 93-space accessory garage to a 185-space public garage with no physical change; CB7 approved 20-10, the BP approved, and only the applicant spoke; CPC focused on parking and traffic.

evidence_summary: The C2-1 overlay enabled a 5000-square-foot restaurant; CB9 approved 21-1 while requesting safer driveway geometry and an eight-foot fence; the applicant committed to fencing, planting, a stop sign, and a no-left-turn sign, but CPC did not resolve every requested design detail.

evidence_summary: This garage was one component of the major Downtown Brooklyn plan; the CB committee opposed the garage permits, the BP imposed extensive conditions, 33 CPC speakers opposed parts of the plan, and CPC adopted several revisions and mitigation procedures while rejecting other demands.

Civic groups appeared on both sides; opposition is coded because the schema has no mixed category.

evidence_summary: The 88-block contextual rezoning primarily restricted multifamily development in response to requests from civic groups, CB13, and the BP zoning task force; CB13 approved 30-0 and a local resident supported the preservation goal.
coder_notes: Literal zoning is mixed because limited R4B and commercial-overlay changes increase or legalize capacity, but the dominant practical effect is lower.

evidence_summary: CB4 unanimously opposed an illegally operated garage after block-association complaints about sidewalk storage and congestion; the BP conditioned approval on evicting the operator; the owner terminated the contract and proposed safety changes, but CPC denied the permit on traffic and layout grounds.
coder_notes: The CPC hearing had no opposition speakers, but the unanimous CB disapproval and documented block-association complaints establish substantial local opposition.

evidence_summary: A Council member sponsored a waterfront downzoning to preserve detached housing; the BP sought removal of attached-house areas and two building-industry speakers opposed on nonconformance, process, and affordable-housing grounds; CPC expressly rejected those objections and approved.

evidence_summary: The R1-2 to R1-1 rezoning limited lot subdivision to implement CB8 preservation-plan goals; CB8 approved 24-0, and the Council member, BP representative, CB land-use chair, and Riverdale Nature Preservancy all supported it.

evidence_summary: The 161-block contextual rezoning primarily reduced development flexibility in response to community, CB, BP, and elected-official concerns; after one homeowner objected, CPC removed two blockfronts from R2A and retained R3A; CB7 approved 34-1.

evidence_summary: The permit converted and expanded an existing Times Square garage without construction; CB5 and the BP approved, two speakers supported it, and CPC reviewed traffic and pedestrian effects.

evidence_summary: At CB6, civic-association, and elected-official request, the 41-block contextual rezoning restricted future multifamily development; CB6 approved 31-0 and the civic-association president supported it at CPC.

evidence_summary: The permit allowed 3617 square feet of retail in an existing three-story building after unsuccessful industrial marketing; CB2 voted 43-0, the BP approved, and no one opposed at CPC.

evidence_summary: The sewage-pump permit was integral to a 97-unit development on a mostly wooded 14-acre site; CB3 approved 19-10 but requested another access point and raised sewer and wetlands concerns; CPC expressly deferred to Fire Department and DEC review and approved.

evidence_summary: A commercial overlay enabled new retail; CB12 unanimously disapproved and six residents opposed on traffic, parking, neighborhood character, and housing-loss grounds; after local testimony the applicant reduced the plan to a one-story bank and considered parking, but CPC approved and rejected remaining objections.

evidence_summary: The permit legalized small ground-floor retail or artist use in an existing building; CB2 approved 38-0, the BP approved, and two speakers supported it.

evidence_summary: The R5B-to-C4-4A extension legalized an existing building and raised another lot to 4.0 FAR; CB15 disapproved 26-9, a neighboring owner opposed height and use effects, and the BP sought deed-limited parking rates; CPC rejected the rate condition as outside scope and approved.

evidence_summary: The C3-to-C8-1 rezoning enabled a 106781-square-foot auto mall; CB18 and the BP approved with extensive traffic, waterfront, landscaping, use, infrastructure, and environmental conditions; applicants made many written commitments and the plan was smaller than an earlier version, while CPC endorsed some and left others beyond scope.

evidence_summary: CB1 approved the 22-space accessory garage 35-5 conditioned on it never becoming public parking; the applicant represented that it would remain accessory-only, and CPC expressly found that response adequate.

evidence_summary: The M1-1 and R6/C1-3 to C8-3 rezoning enabled a 36375-square-foot shopping-center expansion; CB7 and both BPs approved, and the applicant signed traffic and hazardous-material mitigation commitments after environmental review.

evidence_summary: The rezoning enabled a 344-room hotel; CB12 unanimously disapproved and the BP disapproved over concern that it could become a homeless shelter; the applicant produced local support letters and promised a high-quality hotel, but CPC approved without an enforceable use concession.
